nodes.label: new-config
nodes.responsibility: holds the new configuration after mutation

nodes.label: indexing
nodes.responsibility: validates and indexes config objects; on failure restores old config

nodes.label: handoff
nodes.responsibility: initiates replacement by decoding new config and running it

nodes.label: run-new-apps
nodes.responsibility: provisions and starts all apps from new config; on failure stops started apps and returns error

nodes.label: old-config-running
nodes.responsibility: maintains old configuration active until handoff succeeds

nodes.label: restore-old
nodes.responsibility: restores old config on failure and returns error

question_overlay.summary: Caddy preserves the old configuration until the new applications are fully started. The handoff process first validates and indexes the new config (indexing), then decodes and runs it (handoff). If indexing or running the new applications fails, the old config is restored and remains active. Handoff can fail during indexing, during application provisioning/start, or during the finishSettingUp step after start.
unknowns: whether there is a timeout for application startup
whether partial failures of individual apps are handled beyond stopping already-started ones
